name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3240
preamble: Joshua Kosman and Henri Picciotto Share Copy Link Facebook X (Twitter) Bluesky Pocket Email May 15, 2012 This article appears in the June 4, 2012 issue.

clue.text: One found within, riffling a Roget in spring

indicators.note: riffling shuffles pages or cards, so the letters are leafed into a new order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
within means inside, which is in
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone leafs through a thesaurus in springtime and finds a word inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring here is a verb, not the season: to spring from something is to ORIGINATE in it. Roget's is the classic thesaurus.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring from a source is to arise or begin there, a common verb synonym.

clue.text: Visually misconstrue a city poll

indicators.note: to misconstrue is to read something wrongly, so the letters are taken in a wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone misreads the results of an election in a city by looking at them wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical things concern the eye and sight, so the adverb means by means of vision.

clue.text: Spring exists to go to court

blocks.note: is means exists
to sue is to take someone to law

explanation.surface: A legal case: a spring is there and someone wants to litigate over it.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring forth and to issue both mean to come out or emerge, as water from a source.

clue.text: Assign uptime unfairly

indicators.note: something done unfairly is not done straight, so the letters are dealt crookedly

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a computer's running time has been allocated unjustly.
explanation.definitionFit: To impute is to attribute or ascribe blame or credit to someone, a synonym of assign.

clue.text: The way spring arrives, relative to winter: faster, surprisingly, when keeping guard

definitions.text: The way spring arrives, relative to winter

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is an unexpected one, so the letters come out in an unexpected order
keeping means holding on to, so one word is held inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
to ward is to guard, and a ward is one under guard

explanation.surface: A question about seasons: does spring come faster than winter, and does it keep watch?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description: spring comes after winter, so it arrives AFTERWARDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring follows winter in the calendar, so it arrives later, which is the sense of the adverb.

clue.text: Complex poetry incorporating public show

indicators.note: incorporating means containing within its body, so the letters sit inside the run of words

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Intricate verse that includes a public performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' looks like the definition or an anagram signal, but it only supplies the end of the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is short for exposition, a large public exhibition or fair.

clue.text: Dog behind post office in spring

indicators.note: behind says one part follows the other in the reading order

blocks.note: PO is the usual abbreviation for post office
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: A dog trailing behind a mail clerk in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop up is to appear suddenly, like something springing up out of nowhere.

clue.text: At first, painter Lichtenstein captures saucy quality

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the next word only
to capture is to hold inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: the first letter of painter
Roy Lichtenstein was the American pop artist
pert means cheeky or saucy

explanation.surface: The pop artist Lichtenstein first painted something with a cheeky flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: Lichtenstein looks like the European principality, but here it is the painter Roy Lichtenstein, giving his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A property is an attribute or characteristic of something, a synonym of quality.

clue.text: Obama is here, concealing birth certificate, perhaps

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something inside, so one piece is tucked within another

blocks.note: someone who is here is present
a birth certificate is one example of identification

explanation.surface: A nod to the 2012 'birther' claims that Obama was hiding his birth certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface mocks the birther conspiracy theory; the definition is simply Obama, who was then the sitting head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama was the US head of state when this was published, an example of the office.

clue.text: Priest's wrinkled drape

indicators.note: wrinkled cloth is creased out of shape, so the letters are crumpled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleric's creased curtain or vestment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is a familiar word for a priest or chaplain, from Spanish and Italian for father.

clue.text: Drunkard comes back to see drunkard

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way it came, so the word reads right to left

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
to spot is to see

explanation.surface: One drunk returns to visit another.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosspot is an old word for a heavy drinker, one who tosses back his pot of ale.

clue.text: Returning ocean drowns mythical bird in spring

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read from its end
something drowned is submerged inside the water, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the deep is a poetic name for the ocean
the roc is the giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A seasonal flood that swallows a legendary bird.
explanation.walkthrough: As verbs, to spring from and to proceed from both mean to arise out of a source.
explanation.definitionFit: To proceed from something is to issue or originate from it, matching spring as a verb.

clue.text: Animal preserve adopts adjustable rate

indicators.note: adjustable means it can be altered, so the letters are rearranged
to adopt is to take in, so one piece is taken inside the other

blocks.note: to cure meat or fish is to preserve it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wildlife reserve takes on a variable-rate mortgage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal preserve' reads as a wildlife park, but Animal is the definition and preserve is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature is any living being, especially a beast, so it is a general word for an animal.

clue.text: Go for a spin around Egypt's capital in spring

indicators.note: a word's capital is its head, the opening letter
around means encircling, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: to drive somewhere for pleasure is to go for a spin
the first letter of Egypt

explanation.surface: A spring motoring trip around Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: Egypt's capital tempts you towards Cairo; here it means only the first letter of Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: To derive from and to spring from both mean to originate or come out of a source.

clue.text: LA cop eying suspicious shooting target

indicators.note: something suspicious is fishy and not as it seems, so the letters are not in their true order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles police officer watches a suspect who becomes a target for gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: A clay pigeon is the clay disc flung into the air for shotgun target practice.

clue.text: Awfully pale in spring

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters are badly ordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone looking very wan in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap and a spring are both a jump into the air, an everyday synonym.

clue.text: Like the first ruler of Israel, Turner attacked

blocks.note: as means like
Saul was the first king of ancient Israel
Ted Turner is the American media mogul who founded CNN

explanation.surface: A biblical comparison: someone named Turner went on the attack like King Saul.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner suggests the painter or Nat Turner's slave revolt, but it is Ted Turner, founder of CNN.
explanation.definitionFit: Assaulted means made a violent attack on someone, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lester is miscast in Disney movie directed by Oliver Stone

indicators.note: a miscast actor is put in the wrong role, so the letters are put in the wrong places
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: Walt Disney, the studio's founder
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor called Lester is wrongly cast in a Disney film made by Oliver Stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Disney is the man, Walt, not the studio's films.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall Street (1987) is Oliver Stone's film about financial greed, featuring Gordon Gekko.

clue.text: Truck in reverse breaks through the Met, missing the start for recording of The Hours

indicators.note: in reverse means backwards, so the word is read from its end
breaking through something puts one piece in the middle of another
missing the start means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: a semi is the American name for an articulated truck
taken as written
taken as written; the Met is New York's Metropolitan Opera

explanation.surface: A truck crashes into the Metropolitan Opera, losing a recording of Philip Glass's score for the film The Hours.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hours looks like the film or the opera; read literally, it means hours worked, which a TIME SHEET records.
explanation.definitionFit: A time sheet is a form logging the hours an employee has worked.

clue.text: Chooses to restrict leader of impious god-slayers

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the first letter is taken
restricting something holds it in, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: to decide is to choose
the first letter of impious

explanation.surface: Someone chooses to curb the head of an irreverent band of god-killers.
explanation.definitionFit: A deicide is one who kills a god, from Latin deus plus the killing suffix -cide.

clue.text: Definitely strayed off track in past time

definitions.note: the answer is plural: past times

indicators.note: going off track means leaving the proper route, so the letters wander out of order

blocks.note: yes is an emphatic affirmative, definitely
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone certainly wandered off the path at some earlier time.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterdays are days gone by, the former times of the past.

clue.text: Spring arrest

blocks.note: first meaning: to ... from something is to spring from it
second meaning: to ... a flow is to stop it

explanation.walkthrough: Reads like freeing a prisoner and arresting them; both are verbs with quite different senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to originate from (stem from) and to check or halt (stem the bleeding).

clue.text: Scalia drunk with French port

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; Antonin Scalia was a US Supreme Court justice

explanation.surface: A Supreme Court justice tipsy on fortified wine from France.
explanation.walkthrough: Port looks like the drink, which suits drunk; it is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Calais is the ferry port in northern France facing Dover across the Channel.

clue.text: Spring softly, with a little weight

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for softly
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Bounce lightly while carrying a small load.
explanation.definitionFit: To pounce is to leap suddenly upon prey, a kind of spring.

clue.text: Prepares for a trip to proclaim peace

indicators.note: proclaiming is announcing out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: pax is Latin for peace

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a journey in order to announce a truce.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone packs a suitcase before setting off on a journey.

clue.text: Nativism wrecked health needs

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed up, so the letters are broken apart and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A political claim that anti-immigrant sentiment has damaged public healthcare.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitamins are nutrients the body requires to stay well.

clue.text: Silly goose! That's how it ends

blocks.note: surface reading: calling someone a silly goose and declaring the matter finished
setter's reading: the word goose finishes with the letter E, and the answer split into three describes exactly that

explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' is the definition; the rest describes where the final letter of goose sits, a phrase that run together spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means foolish or pointless, a straightforward synonym of silly.

clue.text: Carnivorous 11 rises in spring

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading upward, from bottom to top

blocks.note: 11 is the answer to 11 across, a creature; a carnivorous one is a wolf

explanation.surface: A predator emerges in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 11 across, CREATURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is where water flows from the ground, and both words mean to issue or pour out.

clue.text: Dialect in translation — that would be easy to defend

definitions.text: that would be easy to defend

indicators.note: a translation turns words into another form, so the letters are recast

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that a regional way of speaking, once translated, is easy to justify.
explanation.walkthrough: Defend suggests arguing a case; the definition means a stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress on high ground, built to be easily defended.

clue.text: Marine mammal shifting tail forward in spring

indicators.note: moving the tail to the front takes the final letter round to the start

blocks.note: the manatee is the sea cow

explanation.surface: A sea creature swims tail-first in the spring.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to flow or issue from a source, as to spring from does.

clue.text: Camps in the beginning of spring (March 15, say)

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter alone

blocks.note: the first letter of spring
the Ides of March is 15 March in the Roman calendar

explanation.surface: Groups gathering at the start of spring, around mid-March.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing factions in a dispute are its sides, and camps means the same.

clue.text: Weather-beaten snakes shed tears

blocks.note: a road that snakes winds about
to weep is to shed tears

explanation.surface: Storm-battered serpents weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A windswept place is exposed to strong gales, so it is battered by the elements.
